definition: In natural language processing, textual entailment (TE), also known as natural language inference (NLI), is a directional relation between text fragments.
details: The relation holds whenever the truth of one text fragment follows from another text.

explainer.lead: Also known as natural language inference, it is a directional relation between text fragments that holds whenever the truth of one fragment follows from another. It matters as a core test of whether a system understands how statements imply one another.

tiers.eli5: If one sentence is true, does that force another sentence to be true? That link between two pieces of text is what this term names.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat it as a directional relation and build systems that judge whether one text fragment's truth follows from another. Pitfall: the direction matters, so treating the relation as symmetric gives wrong judgments.
tiers.paperLevel: A directional relation between text fragments that holds whenever the truth of one text fragment follows from another. No formula or limits beyond the directionality are given.

explainer.example: From "a dog is running in the park," it follows that an animal is moving outdoors, so the relation holds in that direction.
